In this lesson you will learn about troubleshooting Schmitt Triggers.
INTRODUCTIONM
The troubleshooting procedures for a Schmitt trigger are not much different from the procedures used to troubleshoot most other transistor circuits.
Schmitt Triggers have relatively few components. This makes troubleshooting easy as compared to other circuits.
An incorrect waveform indicates that the circuit is faulted.
Check the output signal, input signal, Vcc, the transistors, and circuit resistances.
Let's begin the lesson on SCHMITT TRIGGER TROUBLESHOOTING EXPERIMENT........
LESSON MENU
SCHMITT TRIGGER FAULTS
Schmitt Triggers produce an output pulse any time the upper threshold level is exceeded by the input signal.
DISCUSSION
Although they are often used to change irregular wave shapes into clean pulses, troubleshooting is easier with a symmetrical waveform applied.
The input signal must be greater at some point than the threshold of the circuit. If the output is a constant high or low, a fault may exist.
If the output is incorrect and you suspect the circuit is faulted, check the input amplitude.
If the input amplitude does periodically exceed the upper threshold level and the output is incorrect, a problem exists.
Once you have measured the input of the circuit and determined it to be correct, measure Vcc to ensure correct supply voltage.
If Vcc checks good, the next step is to check the transistors in the circuit.
og ohmmeter or a diode junctishould be made with the input signal and Vcc disconnected (zero).
Transistor checks with an analog ohmmeter or a diode junction tester should be made with the input signal and Vcc disconnected (zero).
The Base-to-Emitter and Base-to-Collector junctions should read a high reading for one lead polarity and low reading for the other. It doesn't matter if an an)

The Base-to-Emitter and Base-to-Collector junctions should read a high reading for one lead polarity and low reading for the other. An analog ohmmeter will show resistance flowing in one direction only. A diode junction tester will indicate current flow in only one direction.
If both transistors check good, the next step is to measure the circuit resistances with an ohmmeter. A digital ohmmeter is p

If both transistors check good, the next step is to measure the circuit resistances with an ohmmeter. A digital ohmmeter is preferred as it lacks sufficient voltage to forward bias a transistor junction. But an analog ohmmeter can be used if the leads are positioned to reverse bias the junction. Just reverse the leads if an erroneous reading is displayed.
With Vcc and the input still disconnected, measure from the Vcc input across the circuit resistances.
Individual circuit resistances may also need to be made such as R6, R2, etc. This step of troubleshooting is a skill that becomes better with practice.
Sometimes, multiple current paths make resistance measurements difficult.
A digital multimeter helps to ensure that semiconductor components are not forward biased, causing erroneous resistance measurements.
Resistance measurements help to identify shorted or open components.
Is this Schmitt Trigger functioning correctly?
The input exceeds the upper threshold level twice. The Schmitt Trigger should produce two square wave output pulses.

Use this troubleshooting method as a guide to help you troubleshoot Schmitt Trigger circuits.
This is not the only method. You may develop your own techniques as you become a proficient troubleshooter.

1. A Schmitt Trigger is faulted when the output is a constant high or low and the input exceeds the threshold.
2. If a fault is suspected, check the input to ensure it periodically exceeds the threshold.
3. If the input is correct, check Vcc to ensure proper supply voltage.
4. Then perform junction tests of the transistors with an analog ohmmeter or digit.
4. Then perform junction tests of the transistors with an analog ohmmeter or digital junction tester.
